title: Moses
summary: Levite, son of Amram and Jochebed; led Israel out of Egypt at 80 (Exod 7:7); died at 120 (Deut 34:7).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (F. N. Jones): 1571 BC (Moses born) (no higher-tier year available).

birth.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), Chart Three §C, p. 56 ("1491 + 80 = 1571 BC (Moses born)")
Ussher, Annals of the World, Third Age §162 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

birth.date: "2433 - Moses ben Amram born (Amram and Jochebed are 83)"
birth.citation: Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 5)," Biblical Chronology 6:7 (July 1994), §15 "Moses" (year list)
Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 6, chart "Year of the World: From Joseph’s death to the Judges"
birth.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2433.

birth.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 5 "The Egyptian Empire (2450–332 BC)", PDF p. 141 (printed p. 140)
birth.note: The Timeline Review (p. 166) prints "1571/1526* bc" (the order is reversed: here the asterisked year is the book's own); p. 456 prints "Jochebed Gives Birth to Moses 1440 bc". Differs from the sort year (1571 BC, ussher-jones) by 45 years.
birth.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "c. 1571 BC" (PDF p. 217): 45 years earlier.

birth.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 9 "Early Egypt and the Exodus of God's People", PDF p. 217 (printed p. 203)
Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 783b
birth.note: Year cell "3116 2434 351". The third printed figure 351 is the column "Promise", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 120 at the end of the name is the lifespan he prints. His table also prints the death at World 2553. 2434 + 120 is not 2553. Both figures are left as printed.

birth.date: Moses was borne in the yeere of the World 2434.
birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Book II, ch. IIII, §I, sig. 184a
birth.note: Narrative sentence. The chronological table prints the same yeere of the World. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. No BC conversion.

birth.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxiii

death.note: Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.

death.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §297 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

death.date: 1st day of the 11th month, year 2554 ("months 7-10, 2554 ... the 1st day of the 11th month ... apparently on that same day, Moses died")
death.citation: Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 6)," Biblical Chronology 6:8 (August 1994), §18 "The Years 2553 and 2554"
death.note: Jordan's year here turns at the 7th month (autumn). BC 2:8 has "AM 2553 End of 40 years in wilderness". Same account in A Chronological and Calendrical Commentary on the Pentateuch (No. 3, 2001), ch. 19 "The Years 2553 and 2554", p. 53: "This brings us to the 1st day of the 11th month ... apparently on that same day, Moses died"; No. 2 (2001), p. 51 list: "2554 - Beginning of Conquest of the land."

death.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 3, chart "Genesis 12 – 25 Chronology of Abraham’s Life"
death.note: Differs from Jordan's own published figure(s): AM 2554.

death.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 10 "The Beginning of Babylon–First of the Mesopotamian Empires", PDF p. 247 (printed p. 233)
Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 784b
death.note: Year cell "3235 2553 40". The third printed figure 40 is the column "Exodus", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. Book II, sig. 206b prints "which happened in the yeere of the World 25 54", with a space in the figures. That spaced figure is not entered as a year. The table row entered is "The Last yeere of Moses." at World 2553.

reign.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

reign.date: “Amos; in whose time Moses went forth from Egypt”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 119; Manetho, ap. Syncellus, Chronicon 59 to 75, and Eusebius, Chronicle 15 to 17
reign.note: First of the eighteenth dynasty in this list. No reign length is printed. Not attached to Ahmose I. The text does not spell the name Amosis here.

reign.date: “his name was changed, and he was called Moyses (Mouses or Moses)”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 135; Manetho, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: This sentence is in the fragment. The editorial footnote on p. 132 ('By Osarsiph he means Moses') was not used. Osarsiph was not given a record. No reign length is printed.

reign.date: “this same period for the interval between Moses and Solomon”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 99; Julius Africanus, in the editor's biographical notice (the notice says it is abridged from Bunsen)
reign.note: Editor's summary in the biographical notice, which says it is abridged from Bunsen. Not a verbatim fragment. The year of the world is left in the quotation. It is not stored and it is not converted. The same 1020 years.

reign.date: “in the reign of Apis, the son of Phoroneus”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 146; Polemo, ap. Africanus, ap. Eusebius, Praeparatio Evangelica, book 10
reign.note: A part of the Egyptian army went to Palestine. The next sentence says these were they who went out with Moses. Apis is not given a record. No year is printed.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 147; Artabanus, ap. Eusebius, Praeparatio evangelica, book 10
reign.note: Artabanus. Scripture gives forty years. No scripture link was added by hand.

reign.date: “he was in the eighty-ninth year of his age”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 148; Artabanus, ap. Eusebius, Praeparatio evangelica, book 10
reign.note: Artabanus, of Moyses, when he did these things. An age, not a reign length. Exodus 7:7 says Moses was eighty years old when he spoke to Pharaoh. No scripture link was added by hand. The italic sentence that Artabanus wrote about a century before Christ is the editor's and was not entered.
